What is the $y$-intercept of the parabola shown above?
worked_solution:
First, we need to find the equation of the parabola. From the diagram, we see that the parabola has a vertex at $(5,15)$ and passes through the point $(2,6).$

The general standard equation of an up- or down-opening parabola with vertex at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
(x-h)^{2}=4p(y-k),
$$

and substituting $(h,k)=(5,15)$ into the above gives

$$
(x-5)^{2}=4p(y-15).
$$

Now, we need to find $p.$ Since the parabola passes through the point $(2,6),$ we substitute $x=2$ and $y=6$ into the equation and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(2-5)^{2} & =4p(6-15) \\ 9 & =4p(-9) \\ p & =-\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the parabola is

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-5)^{2} & =-(y-15).\end{aligned}
$$

When the parabola intersects the $y$-axis, we must have $x=0.$ So, we substitute $x=0$ into the equation of the parabola and solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(0-5)^{2} & =-(y-15) \\ 25 & =-y+15 \\ y & =15-25 \\ y & =-10\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $y$-intercept is $-10.$
